title: Reverse in Groups
statement:
Reverse a singly linked list in consecutive blocks of `k` nodes, leaving a final block that is shorter than `k` untouched.

Contract
- Walk the list from the head, taking blocks of exactly `k` nodes. Reverse the order of the nodes inside each full block; a trailing block with fewer than `k` nodes keeps its original order.
- Rearrange the existing nodes by relinking `next` pointers. Do not create new nodes and do not just swap the `val` fields; callers compare node identity.
- Return the new head. A null list returns null. If `k` is larger than the list, nothing changes.
- Throw `IllegalArgumentException` when `k < 1`. With `k == 1` the list is unchanged.
- Use O(1) extra space beyond the list itself.

Examples
- `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5` with `k = 2` becomes `2 -> 1 -> 4 -> 3 -> 5`.
- `1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6` with `k = 3` becomes `3 -> 2 -> 1 -> 6 -> 5 -> 4`.
- `1 -> 2 -> 3` with `k = 1` stays `1 -> 2 -> 3`.
hints: Reversing a whole list means flipping every `next` pointer as you walk. Doing it for one block of k nodes is the same loop, run k times, but you must reconnect the block to its neighbours.

Before reversing a block, check that k nodes really remain; if not, stop and leave the tail alone. Remember the node before the block, the block's first node (which becomes its last), and the node just after the block.

Start the reversal with `prev` set to the node after the block, so the block's old first node ends up pointing at the rest of the list automatically. Then point the previous block's tail at the block's new first node and move on. A dummy node before the head removes the head special case. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: list values, then | and the group size, for example: 1 2 3 4 5 | 2
